explanation: The closest Mathlib result is Subspace.forall_mem_dualAnnihilator_apply_eq_zero_iff (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Lemmas.lean). It says v ∈ W ↔ ∀ φ ∈ W.dualAnnihilator, φ v = 0. The library's proof already uses it. The target is a basis-indexed version: it tests membership only against the elements of a basis b of the dual annihilator. Getting from the Mathlib lemma to the target needs an extra argument. You must show that the evaluation functional at x, restricted to the annihilator, vanishes because it vanishes on a basis (Basis.ext). That is more than one or two short lines. I grepped Dual/Defs.lean, Dual/Lemmas.lean and the rest of Mathlib for dualAnnihilator combined with Basis or span and found no basis-indexed membership lemma.
